headline: The official same-point comparison still runs well below the polls: against 2022, Florida (D+4.5 by registration after its first in-person ballots, vs. a mail-only D+4.0 at 15 days out in 2022) and Iowa pool to an implied national vote of about R+0.6 (±2.1), while Nevada's first match with 2024 (D+8.0 vs. R+3.2) implies D+6.9, against polls at D+7.9. News comparisons lean more Democratic: Democrats won Clark County's first in-person day after losing it by 8 in 2022, Georgia's turnout has caught up with 2022's pace, and Republicans are 20% of North Carolina's early voters vs. 30% at this point in 2022, though Democrats moving from mail to in person bends every comparison.

measures.label: Iowa: early voters by registration, D-minus-R margin (mail plus in person)
measures.src: Call the Map (Iowa Secretary of State daily absentee statistics), Oct 18
measures.aff: Independent tracker of the official files; affiliation not stated. 33,418 ballots through Oct 15, mostly cast in person, vs. the same point in 2024 (D+10.4 at the same point in 2022)

measures.label: Pennsylvania: returned mail ballots by registration, D-minus-R margin (52 comparable counties)
measures.src: Call the Map (Pennsylvania Department of State mail-ballot file), Oct 16
measures.aff: Independent tracker of the official file; affiliation not stated. 52 of 67 counties (92% of ballots); the app's own comparison takes over once the 2024 baseline reaches this point

measures.label: Maine: absentee ballots by registration, D-minus-R margin
measures.src: Call the Map (Maine Secretary of State absentee file), Oct 18
measures.aff: Independent tracker of the official file; affiliation not stated. 96,849 ballots through Oct 15 vs. the same point in 2024 (Oct 17, 2024); 2022 at the same working day was D+33.6

measures.label: Florida: returned mail ballots by registration, D-minus-R margin (before in-person voting)
measures.src: Call the Map (Florida Division of Elections file), Oct 18
measures.aff: Independent tracker of the official file; affiliation not stated. 830,964 ballots through Oct 17 vs. the same day in 2024 (count 29% below 2024); D+3.9 at the same point in 2022. The app's official comparison takes over once its 2024 baseline reaches this point

measures.label: Virginia: Democratic share of early voters, two-party (L2 modeled party)
measures.aff: L2 is a nonpartisan commercial vendor; Virginia has no party registration, so party is modeled in both years

measures.label: Ohio: early voters by party (last primary ballot), D-minus-R margin
measures.src: News 5 Cleveland, Oct 13 (Ohio Secretary of State data)

compare_note: Registered-party margin among early ballots, 2026 vs. the same point in 2024, as read from the official files by Call the Map (an independent tracker; Iowa 33,418 ballots through Oct 15, Pennsylvania's 52 comparable counties through Oct 16, Maine 96,849 through Oct 15, Florida's mail ballots through Oct 17, before in-person voting). Virginia's early voters are 63% Democratic on L2's modeled two-party split, vs. 59% at the same point in 2024 (Morris, Oct 12); Ohio's early voters were 41% Democratic and 28% Republican by last primary ballot as of Oct 13, vs. 26% and 36% at this point in 2024 (News 5 Cleveland, from Secretary of State data). Florida's, Nevada's, Colorado's, Iowa's, Pennsylvania's and North Carolina's official comparisons with 2022 and 2024 are computed from the state files above. Every state with party registration is more Democratic than at this point in 2024 except Florida, which is level; against 2022 the picture is mixed and narrowing.

bullets.title: Florida's first in-person ballots pulled its gap down to D+4.5, close to 2022's, and the official comparison stays far below the polls.
bullets.html: By registration, the Division of Elections' Oct 19 file counts 1,021,807 ballots at D+4.5, down from D+6.1 the day before: the 116,867 in-person ballots in it were 45,048 Democrats and 49,651 Republicans. At 15 days out in 2022 the gap was D+4.0 on 1,164,753 mail ballots, counted the morning in-person voting began, so the 2026 figure already carries a day of in-person votes that 2022's lacks. The app's calibrated slope turns the 0.5-point difference into about 0.4 points of margin (±2.4); pooled with Iowa, the official comparison with 2022 implies a national vote of about R+0.6 (±2.1), against polls at D+7.9. Nevada's first match with 2024 points the other way: D+8.0 on 77,590 ballots, nearly all mail, against R+3.2 at the same point in 2024, when two days of in-person voting were already in, implying about D+6.9 (±2.8). Before in-person voting, Florida's mail ballots were D+6.2 against D+6.1 on the same day in 2024 (Call the Map).
sources: Florida Division of Elections via the app's official comparison, Oct 19
Florida Politics, Oct 2022 (as early voting began)
bullets.aff: Official data; Call the Map is an independent tracker

bullets.title: Nevada's first in-person weekend went to Democrats, reversing 2022's Republican start in Clark County.
bullets.html: On the first day of in-person voting, Oct 17, Democrats won Clark County's in-person vote 43-37, after losing day one by 8 points in 2022, on about 3,500 more voters. By the evening of Oct 18 Jon Ralston counted Democrats ahead statewide by 6.3 points and more than 6,500 ballots of about 104,000, leading in both Clark and Washoe and in both mail and in-person voting. Ralston cautions that the Oct 18 update lacked rural numbers, that two days are not a trend, and that Republicans won 2022's Election Day by nearly 50,000 ballots. His Oct 16 model still projects an R+3 electorate.

bullets.title: North Carolina Republicans are 20% of early voters, vs. 30% at this point in both 2022 and 2018.
bullets.html: After three days of in-person voting, registered Republicans were 20% of North Carolina's early voters, against 30% at the same point in 2022 and in 2018, a Democratic wave year (John Locke Foundation tracker, via WFAE). Michael Bitzer counts 525,970 ballots through Oct 18 vs. 383,029 on the same day of 2022 (+37.3%): in-person voting is up 49.3% and mail down 30%. Black non-Hispanic voters are nearly a quarter of in-person ballots against 20% of registration. A right-leaning analyst finds Democrats up most among people who skipped the 2022 midterm.
bullets.aff: Nonpartisan outlet and academic; the John Locke Foundation and Rational Ground are conservative/right-leaning

bullets.title: Georgia's early vote has caught up to 2022 at the same point.
bullets.html: GeorgiaVotes counted 862,780 voters as of Oct 19 (825,966 in person, 36,814 by mail), vs. 844,276 at this point in 2022, 2% higher; on Oct 14 it had been 14% behind. 35.3% of voters are Black, 54.9% are women and 46.8% are 65 or older, and 15.3% did not vote in the 2022 general. The AJC reports turnout soaring in Republican-leaning Cherokee and Forsyth counties and lagging in parts of rural South Georgia. Georgia has no party registration.
bullets.aff: Independent tracker of official files; nonpartisan outlet

bullets.title: Ohio's early electorate has flipped from Republican to Democratic.
bullets.html: Democrats have returned about 94,000 ballots, unaffiliated voters a little more than 67,000 and Republicans nearly 64,000, by last primary ballot (Ohio Capital Journal, from Secretary of State data); News 5 Cleveland put Democrats at 41% and Republicans at 28% of nearly 230,000 early votes as of Oct 13, vs. 26% and 36% at this point in 2024. In-person votes in the first week were 194,841, nearly four times 2022's 50,368, and Cuyahoga, Lucas, Lorain and Summit counties have already passed 40% of their 2022 early-vote totals; but only 631,079 mail ballots have been requested vs. 871,041 at this point in 2022, and seniors are more than half of the ballots cast.
bullets.aff: Official data via a nonpartisan outlet

bullets.title: Turnout without party: Virginia and Minnesota stay ahead of 2022, while Wisconsin's mail vote still lags.
bullets.html: More than 678,000 Virginians had voted by Oct 18, nearly 300,000 more than at the same point in 2022 (VPAP). Minnesota had accepted 202,252 ballots through Oct 15 vs. 172,520 at the same point in 2022, a 17% lead, down from 29% a week earlier. Wisconsin had 173,164 absentee ballots returned as of Oct 19 vs. over 195,287 at the same point in 2022, per WTMJ, though another count put the deficit at 29% on Oct 16; in-person absentee voting there starts Oct 20. Texas opened early voting on Oct 19 with a record 19 million registered voters; no first-day count was available at the time of writing.

bullets.title: The edge over 2024 is real but partly a change in how Democrats vote.
bullets.html: Democratic mail requests in North Carolina are down 40% from 2022, against 18% for Republicans, yet Democrats are returning ballots faster (22% returned vs. 17% in 2022). In Pennsylvania, 30% of the Democrats who had voted early by this point in 2024 have already voted again, vs. 18% of Republicans (L2 data via G. Elliott Morris). In an NBC poll, 23% of Democrats plan to vote by mail, down from 34% in 2024, and 36% plan to vote early in person, up from 30%.
bullets.aff: Nonpartisan; L2 is a nonpartisan commercial vendor

bullets.title: Republicans say they vote later.
bullets.html: National Review's Noah Rothman argues Democrats will lead the early vote, "but perhaps not by the margins the party expects," because their own warnings eroded trust in mail. Ohio Republican strategist Bob Clegg says early voting "really tells you nothing" because Republicans vote later, while acknowledging a turnout problem. Wisconsin's GOP reads the Madison and Milwaukee declines as "a lack of enthusiasm among Dem voters." No quantitative RNC early-vote claims for 2026 turned up.
bullets.aff: GOP-aligned claims, reported by nonpartisan outlets

calendar_note: Florida counties could open in-person early voting Oct 19, and every county must by Oct 24; Nevada's in-person early voting opened Oct 17, North Carolina's Oct 15 and Georgia's Oct 13; Minnesota's statewide early voting on tabulators opened Oct 16; Iowa's absentee request deadline is Oct 19. Colorado mailed its ballots Oct 2-9; Oct 19 is when its voter service centers must open. Pennsylvania and New Hampshire have no early in-person voting.
cast_at_note: Ballots counted (UF Election Lab, 40 jurisdictions reporting, state data as of Oct 12-19) when these comparisons were compiled; sets the automatic early-vote weight.
signals_verdict: The official same-point comparison with 2022, still resting on Florida and Iowa, implies a national vote of about R+0.6 (±2.1): Florida's gap narrowed to D+4.5 with the first in-person ballots, half a point more Democratic than 2022's mail-only D+4.0 at 15 days out, while Nevada's first match with 2024 (D+8.0 vs. R+3.2, mail against mail plus in person) implies D+6.9. News comparisons lean further Democratic (Clark County's first in-person day flipped from R+8 in 2022 to D+6, Georgia's total now edges 2022's pace, Maine, Virginia and Minnesota run ahead of 2022), but mail is down and in-person voting up almost everywhere, so the early vote fits a Democratic year without confirming the polls' D+7.9. The next tests are Florida's first in-person week and its first 2024 match, Colorado's first 2022 match, Nevada's first full week in person and Texas's opening days.

signals.title: Democrats won Clark County's first in-person day, which Republicans won by 8 in 2022
signals.value: On the first day of in-person voting (Oct 17), Clark County's in-person voters were 43% Democratic and 37% Republican, which Ralston calls a 14-point turnaround from an 8-point Republican win on day one in 2022, with about 3,500 more voters. Statewide that evening: Democrats 31,767 (39%), Republicans 29,007 (35%), others 21,328 (26%) of 82,102. By the evening of Oct 18 Democrats led statewide by 6.3 points and more than 6,500 ballots of about 104,000, led both Clark and Washoe in mail and in person, and won the day's in-person vote. Over 2022's first weekend, Clark's cumulative in-person vote was D 7,171 (37.2%), R 8,591 (44.6%).
signals.catch: Party is registration, not vote choice. Ralston's counts include ballots returned but not yet accepted, so they run ahead of the state file. His Oct 18 evening update had no rural numbers that day, so it skews Democratic. On Oct 17 Republicans still led the statewide in-person vote by 1.3 points because of the rural counties. His Oct 16 model projects an R+3 electorate (39-36), and he says he will not call a wave after two days. In 2022 Republicans won Election Day by nearly 50,000 ballots.
signals.aff: Nonpartisan outlet (Jon Ralston); county and Secretary of State data

signals.title: Georgia's early vote has caught up with 2022's pace
signals.value: 862,780 voters as of the Oct 19 morning update (825,966 early in person, 36,814 by mail), vs. 844,276 at this point in 2022, 2% higher. That is up from 14% behind on Oct 14. Of these voters, 35.3% are Black, 54.9% are women and 46.8% are 65 or older, and 132,192 (15.3%) did not vote in the 2022 general election.
signals.catch: Georgia has no party registration, so this is turnout, not direction. The AJC reports turnout lagging in parts of rural South Georgia and soaring vs. 2022 in Republican-leaning Cherokee and Forsyth counties. Mail is a far smaller share than in 2022.
signals.aff: GeorgiaVotes is an independent tracker of the Secretary of State's files; AJC is a nonpartisan outlet

signals.title: Ohio's early electorate has flipped from Republican to Democratic
signals.value: Democrats have returned about 94,000 ballots, unaffiliated voters a little more than 67,000 and Republicans nearly 64,000 (by last primary ballot), per the Ohio Capital Journal from Secretary of State data through Oct 12-13; News 5 Cleveland put Democrats at 41% and Republicans at 28% of nearly 230,000 early votes as of Oct 13, vs. 26% and 36% at this point in 2024. In-person votes after one week: 194,841 vs. 50,368 in 2022.
signals.catch: 2024 was a presidential year, and Ohio Republicans are shifting from mail to later voting: mail requests are 631,079 vs. 871,041 at this point in 2022. 'Party' is the last primary ballot pulled; seniors are more than half of ballots so far.
signals.src: Ohio Capital Journal (Ohio Secretary of State data), Oct 15; News 5 Cleveland, Oct 13

signals.title: Virginia's early vote is nearly 300,000 ballots ahead of 2022
signals.value: More than 678,000 Virginians had voted by Oct 18, nearly 300,000 more than at the same point in the 2022 midterm (VPAP data via WTVR). Danville has 2,800 vs. a little over 1,000 in 2022.
signals.catch: Virginia has no party registration, so this is turnout, not direction. The count's exact as-of day is not stated. The modeled party lean is in the separate L2 signal.
signals.src: WTVR CBS 6 (Virginia Public Access Project data), Oct 18
signals.aff: Nonpartisan outlet; VPAP is a nonpartisan tracker of state data

signals.title: Virginia's early voters lean further Democratic than in 2024
signals.value: 63% Democratic on L2's modeled two-party split, vs. 59% at the same point in 2024 (378,000 D to 265,000 R then). 46% of 2024's Democratic early voters have already voted again, vs. 35% of Republicans. CNN/Catalist (Oct 1): voters with only Democratic primary history lead those with only GOP history by 18 points, vs. 8 in 2024.
signals.catch: Virginia has no party registration, so party is modeled, and 2024 had a presidential-year electorate.
signals.src: G. Elliott Morris (L2 data), Oct 12; CNN/Catalist, Oct 1
signals.aff: L2 is a nonpartisan commercial vendor; Catalist is a Democratic-aligned vendor

signals.title: Maine's absentee vote is far more Democratic than 2024's and slightly more than 2022's
signals.value: 96,849 ballots through Oct 15 (48,868 by mail, 52,909 in person): 51,810 Democrats (53.5%), 18,713 Republicans (19.3%), 26,326 unaffiliated (27.2%). That is a D+34.2 gap, vs. D+33.6 at the same working day in 2022 and D+21.7 in 2024. Ballots are up 38% on 2022: Democrats +35%, Republicans +25%, unaffiliated +59%.
signals.catch: Registration is not vote choice. The edge over 2022 has narrowed from 1.5 points (through Oct 12) to 0.6. The 2022 match is by working day. The state's newest file could not be read after Oct 18, so the count is four days old.
signals.src: Call the Map (Maine Secretary of State absentee file), Oct 18
signals.aff: Independent tracker of the official file; affiliation not stated

signals.title: Minnesota's accepted ballots are running 17% ahead of 2022
signals.value: 202,252 absentee and mail ballots accepted through Oct 15 (80,870 in person, 121,382 by mail), vs. 172,520 at the same point in 2022. 519,813 ballots distributed vs. 474,935.
signals.catch: Minnesota has no party registration, so this is turnout, not direction. The lead over 2022 has narrowed from 29% (Oct 8). The source is a local news aggregator citing the Secretary of State's Oct 16 report; the report itself was not opened.
signals.src: Minneapolimedia News (Minnesota Secretary of State Oct 16 report), Oct 18
signals.aff: Official data via a local aggregator

signals.title: Pennsylvania's 2024 Democratic early voters are coming back faster
signals.value: 30% of the Democrats who had voted early by this point in 2024 have already voted, vs. 18% of Republicans; of about 153,000 matched early voters, 76% are registered Democrats and 17% Republicans, vs. 66% and 25% at the same point in 2024.
signals.catch: L2's match covers less than half of the 346,932 ballots the state had counted by Oct 14; the official comparison (above) will supersede the party shares once the 2024 baseline reaches this point. Pennsylvania's mail vote is lopsidedly Democratic every year.
signals.aff: L2 is a nonpartisan commercial vendor

signals.title: Pennsylvania's mail vote is less Democratic than at this point in 2022
signals.value: In the 56 counties with comparable files, 454,582 returned mail ballots are D+46.8 by registration vs. D+55.2 at the same point in 2022, with all ballots down 6% (Call the Map, Oct 18).
signals.catch: Pennsylvania's mail vote is lopsidedly Democratic every year and Democrats are shifting to Election Day voting after the party's own warnings about the mail; the official comparison (above) takes over once its 2022 baseline reaches 12 days out. 67% of ballots so far are from voters 65 and over.
signals.src: Call the Map (Pennsylvania Department of State mail-ballot file), Oct 18
signals.aff: Independent tracker of the official file; affiliation not stated

signals.title: Wisconsin's mail vote still trails 2022, by 11% to 29% depending on the count
signals.value: WTMJ, citing the Elections Commission, reports 173,164 absentee ballots returned of 364,888 requested as of Oct 19, vs. over 195,287 returned and 438,673 requested at the same point in 2022. WRJN puts statewide returns down 29% (Oct 16, 2026 vs. Oct 21, 2022). Racine County has 5,025 vs. 6,472 (-22%).
signals.catch: The two counts disagree on the size of the gap, and WTMJ gives no 2022 as-of date. No party registration. In-person absentee voting starts Oct 20, and both parties are pushing voters away from mail.
signals.src: WTMJ (Wisconsin Elections Commission data), Oct 19; WRJN, Oct 18

signals.title: Michigan's mail returns have fallen back to the 2022 pace
signals.value: 440,677 ballots returned by Oct 13, vs. 432,960 at the same point in 2022; a week earlier returns were 30% ahead. Requests are up more than 20% (2,083,240 vs. 1,707,970).
signals.catch: Michigan has no party registration, so this measures turnout, not direction. About 95% of requests come from the permanent mail list; in-person early voting opens Oct 24.
